import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Infinitude of Wall–Sun–Sun primes

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_prime)
-/

open Algebra (IsQuadraticExtension)
open NumberField

namespace QuadraticAlgebra
variable {d : ℤ} [Fact <| Squarefree d] [Fact <| d ≠ 1]

/-- The discriminant of `ℚ[√d]` for `d ≥ 2` squarefree congruent to 1 mod 4 is `d`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11, simp]
lemma discr_rat_of_modEq_one (hd₄ : d ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4]) : discr (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) = d := by
  sorry

/-- The discriminant of `ℚ[√d]` for `d ≥ 2` squarefree not congruent to 1 mod 4 is `4 * d`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11, simp]
lemma discr_rat_of_not_modEq_one (hd₄ : ¬ d ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4]) :
    discr (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) = 4 * d := by
  sorry

end QuadraticAlgebra

namespace Algebra
variable {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]

variable (K L) in
/-- A quadratic algebra `L` over a field `K` is isomorphic to the explicit quadratic algebra
`QuadraticAlgebra K a b` for some `a b : K`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension [IsQuadraticExtension K L] :
    ∃ a b, Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a b) := by
  sorry

/-- An algebra `L` is quadratic over a field `K` iff it is isomorphic to the explicit quadratic
algebra `QuadraticAlgebra K a b` for some `a b : K`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma isQuadraticExtension_iff_exists_quadraticAlgebra :
    IsQuadraticExtension K L ↔ ∃ a b, Nonempty (L ≃ₐ[K] QuadraticAlgebra K a b) where
  mp _ := exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension ..
  mpr := by rintro ⟨a, b, ⟨e⟩⟩; sorry

end Algebra

namespace NumberField
variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]

variable (K) in
/-- A quadratic number field `K` is isomorphic to the explicit quadratic field
`QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0` for some squarefree `d : ℤ` not equal to 1. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension [IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K] :
    ∃ d ≠ (1 : ℤ), Squarefree d ∧ Nonempty (K ≃+* QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) := by
  sorry

/-- A number field `K` is quadratic iff it is isomorphic to the explicit quadratic field
`QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0` for some squarefree `d : ℤ` not equal to 1. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma isQuadraticExtension_iff_exists_quadraticAlgebra :
    IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K ↔
      ∃ d ≠ (1 : ℤ), Squarefree d ∧ Nonempty (K ≃+* QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) where
  mp _ := exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension _
  mpr := by rintro ⟨d, hd₁, hd, ⟨e⟩⟩; sorry

/-- An integer `D` is a fundamental discriminant iff it is the discriminant of the explicit
quadratic field `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0` for some squarefree `d : ℤ` not equal to 1. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma isFundamentalDiscr_iff_exists_discr_quadraticAlgebra {D : ℤ} :
    IsFundamentalDiscr D ↔ ∃ (d : ℤ) (_ : Fact <| d ≠ 1) (_ : Fact <| Squarefree d),
      discr (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ d 0) = D where
  mp := by
    rintro (⟨⟨d, rfl⟩, hD₄, hD⟩ | ⟨hD₁, hD₄, hD⟩)
    · simp only [ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true, mul_div_cancel_left₀] at hD hD₄
      have : Fact <| d ≠ 1 := ⟨by rintro rfl; simp at hD₄⟩
      have : Fact <| Squarefree d := ⟨hD⟩
      exact ⟨d, inferInstance, inferInstance, QuadraticAlgebra.discr_rat_of_not_modEq_one hD₄⟩
    · have : Fact <| D ≠ 1 := ⟨hD₁⟩
      have : Fact <| Squarefree D := ⟨hD⟩
      exact ⟨D, inferInstance, inferInstance, QuadraticAlgebra.discr_rat_of_modEq_one hD₄⟩
  mpr := by
    rintro ⟨d, _, _, rfl⟩; by_cases hd₄ : d ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4] <;> simp [*, IsFundamentalDiscr, Fact.out]

/-- An integer `D` is a fundamental discriminant iff it is the discriminant of some number field. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
lemma isFundamentalDiscr_iff_exists_discr_numberField {D : ℤ} :
    IsFundamentalDiscr D ↔
      ∃ (K : Type) (_ : Field K) (_ : NumberField K), IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K ∧ discr K = D := by
  rw [isFundamentalDiscr_iff_exists_discr_quadraticAlgebra]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨d, _, _, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨_, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, rfl⟩
  · rintro ⟨K, _, _, _, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨d, hd₁, hd, ⟨e⟩⟩ := exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension K
    have : Fact <| d ≠ 1 := ⟨hd₁⟩
    have : Fact <| Squarefree d := ⟨hd⟩
    exact ⟨d, inferInstance, inferInstance, discr_eq_discr_of_ringEquiv _ e.symm⟩

end NumberField

namespace WallSunSun

/--
A prime $p$ is a Wall–Sun–Sun prime if and only if $L_p \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$, where $L_p$ is the
$p$-th Lucas number. It is conjectured that there is at least one Wall–Sun–Sun prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem exists_isWallSunSunPrime : ∃ p, IsWallSunSunPrime p := by
  sorry

/--
A prime $p$ is a Wall–Sun–Sun prime if and only if $L_p \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$, where $L_p$ is the
$p$-th Lucas number. It is conjectured that there are infinitely many Wall-Sun-Sun primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime : {p : ℕ | IsWallSunSunPrime p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
A Lucas–Wieferich prime associated with $(a,b)$ is an odd prime $p$, not dividing $a^2 - 4b$, such
that $U_{p-\varepsilon}(a,b) \equiv 0 \pmod{p^2}$ where $U(a,b)$ is the Lucas sequence of the first
kind and $\varepsilon$ is the Legendre symbol $\left({\tfrac {a^2-4b}{p}}\right)$.
The discriminant of this number is the quantity $a^2 - 4b$. It is conjectured that there are
infinitely many Lucas–Wieferich primes of any given non-one fundamental discriminant.

TODO: Source this conjecture
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq {D : ℤ} (hD : IsFundamentalDiscr D)
    (hD₁ : D ≠ 1) :
    {p : ℕ | ∃ a b, a ^ 2 - 4 * b = D ∧ IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end WallSunSun

findings.description: The existentially chosen Lucas parameters do not define Wall–Sun–Sun primes of the fixed quadratic field. In fact, under hD, the displayed set equals `{p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd p ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D}`. For every such p, the index p − J(D | p) is even, and a divides U_{2n}(a,b). If D ≡ 0 mod 4, choose a = 0 and b = −D/4; if D ≡ 1 mod 4, choose a = p² and b = (p⁴ − D)/4. The required p²-divisibility is then automatic. I proved this set equality and the entire infinitude assertion in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry or reliance on the conjectural declarations. There is also a small mismatch with the claimed D = 5 specialization: a = 7, b = 11, p = 3 satisfies the displayed predicate, since U₄(7,11) = 189 is divisible by 9, but 3 is not a Wall–Sun–Sun prime (L₃ = 4). Both facts were proved in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, “Wall–Sun–Sun primes with discriminant D,” says that the conventional Wall–Sun–Sun primes have D = 5 and conjectures infinitely many Wall–Sun–Sun primes for each non-one fundamental discriminant: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_prime#Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_primes_with_discriminant_D . Its cited primary reference, Elsenhans–Jahnel, arXiv:1006.0824v1, Remark 2.2.8, defines the real-quadratic-field notion using a fundamental unit ε of the fixed field, not arbitrary Lucas parameters with the same polynomial discriminant.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the existential Lucas-parameter predicate by a properly sourced field-level Wall–Sun–Sun predicate, ensuring that D = 5 specializes to the ordinary predicate. For the real-quadratic version in Elsenhans–Jahnel, fix a fundamental unit ε of the field and require ε^(p−1) ≡ 1 modulo p² when the Legendre symbol is 1, or ε^(2p+2) ≡ 1 when it is −1, with congruences in its ring of integers. Any extension to negative discriminants needs an appropriate definition and reference. Merely moving the arbitrary parameters outside the set is insufficient without further restrictions, since a = 0 already gives degenerate fixed sequences.

findings.description: The docstring says “the discriminant of some number field,” but the Lean statement correctly requires `IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K`. Omitting “quadratic” changes the mathematical characterization; this is a documentation-only error, not a defect in the formal statement.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia’s Quadratic field article, Discriminant section, identifies the discriminants of quadratic fields with the fundamental discriminants other than 1. The Fundamental discriminant reference likewise states that a fundamental discriminant is 1 or the discriminant of a quadratic field: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_field#Discriminant and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_discriminant .
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to “An integer D is a fundamental discriminant iff it is the discriminant of some quadratic number field,” understood with the repository’s convention excluding 1.

reformulations.difference: The witnesses use ring equivalences rather than explicitly ℚ-algebra equivalences, and require squarefree d ≠ 1 without separately stating d ≠ 0. The same witness formulation appears in NumberField.exists_quadraticAlgebra_of_isQuadraticExtension.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every ring equivalence between ℚ-algebras fixes rational scalars and therefore gives a ℚ-algebra equivalence; conversely an algebra equivalence gives a ring equivalence. Also, Squarefree (0 : ℤ) is false, so squarefreeness supplies the omitted nonzero condition. The exact equivalence of these two existential witness conditions was proved as Review.quadratic_witness_equiv in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, without sorry.

reformulations.difference: The repository’s IsFundamentalDiscr predicate excludes 1, whereas the encyclopedic convention includes 1. Thus the lemma states the non-one fundamental-discriminant characterization without a separate D ≠ 1 conjunct.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I defined the source’s numerical criterion, including 1, and proved `IsFundamentalDiscr D ↔ SourceFundamentalDiscr D ∧ D ≠ 1`. Consequently the lemma’s left-hand side is exactly the source’s non-one condition, not an erroneous boundary convention. The predicate equivalence and its substitution into arbitrary biconditional statements were proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1006.0824 — Elsenhans–Jahnel, LaTeX source; especially §2.2, Remark 2.2.8, and §4
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundamental_discriminant — redirected to Discriminant, Fundamental discriminants section
https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1090/S0025-5718-07-01955-2 — bibliographic metadata and attempted PDF location
review.notes: Checked all 11 declarations and their relevant imported definitions. The two ordinary Wall–Sun–Sun conjectures are faithful and remain open according to the cited Wikipedia article; the eight textbook lemmas are mathematically sound. Signed squarefree radicands are legitimate in the discriminant formulas. Boundary tests covered small primes, excluded discriminants 0, 1, 4, and valid positive and negative discriminants. Jacobi versus Legendre notation is harmless for primes, and the integer-to-natural index conversion does not truncate permitted indices. The successful tests are in scratch.lean, boundaries.lean, helperchecks.lean, and equivalences.lean under /workspace/review/. The main triviality proof and concrete counterexample proofs have no sorryAx dependency. No repository files were edited. The McIntosh–Roettger AMS PDF was inaccessible; no conclusion relies on having read it.

submission.summary: Replaced the arbitrary Lucas parameters with unit congruences in the ring of integers of a fixed real quadratic field, following Elsenhans–Jahnel. The statement explicitly uses the sourced real-quadratic setting rather than retaining the undefined negative-discriminant extension. Added the primary reference and corrected the minor missing “quadratic” in the discriminant-characterization docstring. Scratch proofs verify equivalence to the fundamental-unit formulation; the required file compilation succeeds with only sorry warnings.

namespace WallSunSun

/--
A prime $p$ is a Wall–Sun–Sun prime if and only if $L_p \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$, where $L_p$ is the
$p$-th Lucas number. It is conjectured that there is at least one Wall–Sun–Sun prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem exists_isWallSunSunPrime : ∃ p, IsWallSunSunPrime p := by
  sorry

/--
A prime $p$ is a Wall–Sun–Sun prime if and only if $L_p \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$, where $L_p$ is the
$p$-th Lucas number. It is conjectured that there are infinitely many Wall-Sun-Sun primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime : {p : ℕ | IsWallSunSunPrime p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
Every real quadratic number field `K` of discriminant `D` is conjectured to have infinitely many
Wall–Sun–Sun primes. These are odd primes $p \nmid D$ for which a fundamental unit $\varepsilon$
satisfies $\varepsilon^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ if $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right) = 1$, and
$\varepsilon^{2p+2} \equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$ if $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right) = -1$.

The congruences are in the ring of integers of `K`. Equivalently, we require them for every
unit: each unit of a real quadratic field is a signed integral power of a fundamental unit,
and both exponents are even.

See [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_prime#Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_primes_with_discriminant_D)
for the conjecture and [Elsenhans–Jahnel](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.0824), Remark 2.2.8,
for this real-quadratic-field definition.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinite_isWallSunSunPrime_of_disc_eq {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    [IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K] [IsTotallyReal K] {D : ℤ} (hD : discr K = D) :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd p ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D ∧
      ∀ ε : (𝓞 K)ˣ, (p : 𝓞 K) ^ 2 ∣
        (ε : 𝓞 K) ^ (if jacobiSym D p = 1 then p - 1 else 2 * p + 2) - 1}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end WallSunSun
